record.description: Every content-derived value an Audit Record seals is a commitment keyed by the salt of the audit's Reference Payload (DC-4 §5), never a bare digest: withdrawing that Payload destroys the salt and renders these commitments uncheckable at the same instant as the Delta's own.

auditor_id.description: The hostname the Auditor was admitted under: DC-4 §3 requires it to be byte-identical to the `subject` of the `auditor_admit` covering `sig.key_id`, and the pattern is the one that `subject` carries, so a Record cannot claim a shape no admission could have.

robots_excluded.description: Present only on an `unreachable` Record whose fetch was forbidden by robots.txt (DC-4 §5); it is what the unauditable horizon counts, so it distinguishes a URL nobody may check from one that was merely down.

then.comment: similarity is required for every change type alike, `delete` included: what the change type adjusts is the reading (DC-4 §5's effective similarity), never the presence of the field, which is what keeps §7's severity derivable for every Confirmed Inconsistency.

allOf.comment: robots_excluded says why a fetch produced no representation, so it belongs to `unreachable` and to nothing else: on any other verdict a representation was obtained (DC-4 §5), and on `not_auditable` the obstacle was the Reference Payload rather than the URL.
